I had a couple of unsuccessful attempts at marmalade and the marmalade separated in the jar with all the jelly on the bottom and the peel on top. It tasted good but it wasn't presentable so I gave up. My friend is getting married and I offered to make her jelly as guest gifts for her wedding. Was really surprised and concerned when she chose marmalade but I studied up on it and learned how to do it the old fashioned way mostly (I skip the overnight soak and still have a very good marmalade).

Get your self 6 or 7 oranges, a quart of water, a cup of lemon juice and five cups of sugar.

Cut the peels of the orange and put them in a bowl. Then remove the pith and seeds from the orange and chop it up good- put it in the pot you'll be making the jam in. Once all the oranges are cut up, turn the stove on med-high and add the lemon juice and water. Let this fast boil for 20 minutes while you slice the orange peels pretty and thin. After about 20 minutes, add the peels and sugar. This isn't like normal jelly. You're gonna want to pull a stool up to the stove because now it cooks for a long time. Let it just cook down until you can scrape the bottom of the pan and it takes a second to disappear (do you know what I mean?).

This recipe yields 6 1.5 pint jars.

It's delicious.

Edit: You're going to gradually turn down the temp the more reduced it gets. Don't want to make candy!
